nodes.question: How did Hicks & Temizel-Sekeryan categorize the potential environmental benefits of nanosilver products?
nodes.answer: Hicks & Temizel-Sekeryan categorized the benefits into three groups: human behavioral benefits, passive benefits, and replacement benefits.
nodes.paragraph: Next to these methods there are also materials which already have an antibacterial activity. In this work, we use AgNP. The antimicrobial efficacy of silver is enhanced at nanoscale, i.e., when the dimension of silver is < 100 nm [ 14]. The Nanotechnology Products Database [ 15], lists the current use of silver in products by relative market share for each industrial division. The largest share falls to the medical applications (24%) which include bandages, catheters, and creams. Textiles are in second place (17.6%), followed by cosmetics (13.4%), and home appliances (9.4%) [ 15].
